text: In Tokyo, you can hire a man to do absolutely nothing.
In twenty-eighteen, Shoji Morimoto was fired. His boss said he didn't do anything useful.
So he made that his job.
He waits at a marathon finish line.
He rides the same train loop for seventeen hours.
He waves goodbye at the station.
He sits in a cafe while a woman hands in her divorce papers.
He barely talks. He just stays.
He says people need the presence of one human being.
Jenny is always there, day or night, even when you just need company.
